    A big thank you to the team at MongoDB for organizing such an engaging and insightful event. As we prepare for upcoming projects, the sessions on document modeling, indexing, query optimization, and schema design provided plenty of ideas to take back and apply in the real world. Being a cricket fan, I couldn’t resist drawing a parallel: 🏏 Every successful project starts with a strong opening partnership — just like a well-designed data model. 🏏 Smart indexing helps find the gaps in the field and keeps the scoreboard moving. 🏏 Query optimization turns good shots into boundaries. 🏏 And when architecture, performance, and scalability come together, that’s when you hit a clean six into the stands. The cricket bat I received at the event makes for a perfect reminder that success comes from preparation, teamwork, and executing the basics well — whether on the cricket field or while building modern data platforms. Looking forward to putting these learnings into action in our future MongoDB-powered initiatives. Thank you again to everyone involved for a fantastic experience. #MDBxNatwest Ravi Khabar NatWest Group Tyl by NatWest

    Celebrating 10 Years at Boeing! This week marks a significant milestone in my career — completing 10 incredible years with Boeing, all spent within the IT&DA(IDT&S) organization, specifically in the Product Systems division (Engineering and Product Support). It’s been a journey filled with learning, growth, and transformation, both personally and professionally. Boeing has truly shaped me by providing unparalleled opportunities for growth and development—opportunities that are hard to match anywhere else. I am grateful for the environment that challenges, supports, and empowers me to continuously evolve. I am deeply grateful to all the leaders, mentors, colleagues, and teams who have supported and inspired me along the way. Your guidance, collaboration, and trust have been instrumental in shaping my path and enabling me to contribute to Boeing’s innovation and success. One of the most rewarding aspects of this journey has been helping to grow the careers of many talented individuals. Seeing others develop, succeed, and take on leadership roles has been a true privilege and a source of immense pride. I will not be doing justice by naming just a few people who have been part of this incredible journey — every interaction and relationship has contributed to where I am today. I also want to sincerely thank all my stakeholders, both internal and external, for their continuous support and partnership throughout this journey. Special thanks to Lucia C., Shashank Jha, Adam Marshall, Jeff Stein, Gail Carr, Paul Dodd, Jennifer Davis for your unwavering support and encouragement. Together, we have achieved remarkable milestones, and I look forward to continuing this journey of driving transformation and delivering value. Here’s to many more years of innovation, leadership, and making a difference at Boeing! #BoeingProud #BoeingLeadership #BoeingInnovation #BoeingCareers #TeamBoeing #BoeingIT #EngineeringAtBoeing #BoeingIDTS

    Swiggy pays around ₹30–45 LPA for Senior Frontend Engineers. This is the actual interview structure they follow: 𝗥𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱 𝟭: 𝗝𝗮𝘃𝗮𝗦𝗰𝗿𝗶𝗽𝘁 + 𝗥𝗲𝗮𝗰𝘁 𝗙𝘂𝗻𝗱𝗮𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗮𝗹𝘀: They expect you to be rock solid on: - Closures, promises, async/await - Event loop (microtasks vs macrotasks) - React state, props, hooks, lifecycle - Common pitfalls with `useEffect` 𝗥𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱 𝟮: 𝗠𝗮𝗰𝗵𝗶𝗻𝗲 𝗖𝗼𝗱𝗶𝗻𝗴: Common tasks: - File explorer with nested folders (recursion) - API-driven list with pagination / “Show More” - Autosuggest search with debounce They judge: - Component structure - State ownership - Edge cases - Code readability 𝗥𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱 𝟯: 𝗙𝗿𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗻𝗱 𝗦𝘆𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗺 𝗗𝗲𝘀𝗶𝗴𝗻: Topics they go deep into: - How React works internally - Virtual DOM, Fiber, hydration - Avoiding unnecessary re-renders - CSR vs SSR tradeoffs - BFF pattern in large-scale apps 𝗥𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱 𝟰: 𝗛𝗶𝗿𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗠𝗮𝗻𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗿 / 𝗢𝘄𝗻𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗵𝗶𝗽: They test: - How you think before coding - What questions you ask from a vague requirement - Performance, caching, extensibility - Testing, monitoring, failure scenarios Example: “𝗗𝗲𝘀𝗶𝗴𝗻 𝗮𝗻 𝗮𝘂𝘁𝗼𝘀𝘂𝗴𝗴𝗲𝘀𝘁 𝗶𝗻𝗽𝘂𝘁 𝘂𝘀𝗲𝗱 𝗮𝗰𝗿𝗼𝘀𝘀 𝗦𝘄𝗶𝗴𝗴𝘆.” Big PBCs don’t hire frontend engineers who just 𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝗱 𝘀𝗰𝗿𝗲𝗲𝗻𝘀, they hire engineers who 𝗼𝘄𝗻 𝗳𝗲𝗮𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗲𝘀 𝗲𝗻𝗱-𝘁𝗼-𝗲𝗻𝗱.   People are getting these roles right now because they prepared for 𝘁𝗵𝗶𝘀 𝘀𝘁𝗿𝘂𝗰𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗲. Most people didn’t. That’s the difference.

Solving 500 LC questions is not a win, because solutions to all LC problems are either available online or can be easily solved with AI

    Amazon, Atlassian and now Oracle. Three major IT giants have conducted major layoffs in just 3 months of 2026. This move will backfire heavily. 1) In 2024, Klarna, the Swedish fintech giant, paused hiring and eventually cut its workforce from roughly 5,500 to 3,400, then quietly rehired humans and acknowledged that while AI handles volume, humans are essential for quality. 2) In 2024 and 2025, IBM paused hiring for roughly 8,000 back-office and HR roles and laid off thousands of senior, higher-salaried workers, followed by the announcement to triple its junior hiring for software developers and HR. 3) In mid-2025, the Commonwealth Bank announced it would replace 45 customer service roles with a proprietary AI voice bot to handle complex inquiries, followed by making a public U-turn and rehiring the terminated employees. The training and running costs of LLMs are mammoth and unsustainable; the companies outsourcing their models and companies investing in AI are eventually going to lose tremendous resources. According to Forrester, 55% of employers who conducted AI-related layoffs in 2024 already regret the decision. Gartner has predicted that by 2027, 50% of companies that attributed headcount reduction to AI will rehire staff to perform similar functions, often under different titles. The AI bubble burst is right around the corner, and when it happens, employers are going to regret it big time. Thoughts? #AI #Amazon #Oracle #Layoffs
